description:
## Empirical anchor

2026-05-13 surfaced by PRINCIPAL during the substrate-architecture discussion. Engagements progress through distinct operating modes, but the substrate doesn't currently canon the **progression pattern** — when do you transition between modes, what triggers the transition, how does the team know which mode is active.

PRINCIPAL's framing: "the pattern that knows about going from pair programming to the full team to the team running in semi autonomous mode using beadworks to communicate."

## The progression

Three operating modes (existing partial substrate canon at MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §12 and operating-disciplines.md §10):

| Mode | Activity | PRINCIPAL involvement | Coordination |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pair programming (Mode 2)** | Interactive prototyping, scoping, exploration | High — in-the-loop on every decision | Conversational; bw used as durable record but lightweight |
| **Full team (Mode 1)** | Formal gauntlet (DAEDALUS → ARGUS → ADA → VERA → CATO → ZENO) | Decision-points only — phase ratification, ship/no-ship | bw heartbeats at phase transitions; PRINCIPAL surfaces explicit |
| **Semi-autonomous** | Long-running engagements with periodic check-in | Exception-handler only — escalation triggers per directive | Monitor + bw-poll bridge (Arc 24 substrate); radio-check between orchestrators |

The substrate has each mode partially documented but does NOT have:
- The **progression sequence** (typical engagement starts in Mode 2 to scope; transitions to Mode 1 for build; may transition to semi-autonomous for long-running phases)
- The **transition triggers** (what signals "we're ready to formalize"; "we can hand off heads-down"; "PRINCIPAL needs to re-engage")
- The **transition mechanics** (how the team is told which mode is active; how the directive captures the operating-mode for the dispatch; how the mode is changed mid-engagement)
- The **regression pattern** (semi-autonomous → full team → pair programming when escalations require re-engagement)

## The substrate-canon shape

Document the progression pattern in operating-disciplines.md (likely as an extension of the existing §10 HITL/Autonomous content):

- The three modes + their characteristics (mostly already canonized; clean up + cross-link)
- The default progression pattern (Mode 2 → Mode 1 → semi-autonomous as engagement matures)
- Transition triggers (concrete signals + the seat that calls the transition)
- Mode declaration in directives (when authoring an arc directive, the mode is explicit)
- Mid-engagement mode transitions (how to escalate up or down)
- The downward-propagation rule (parent seat's mode propagates to dispatched subagents unless explicitly overridden — already canonized in Arc 21 A4)

## Substrate touch-points

- `substrate/operating-disciplines.md` — extension of existing §10 + §11 sections on HITL/Autonomous and autonomous-mode-setup. Adds progression discipline.
- `substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md` — POLYBIUS-specific framing on when to call mode transitions
- `substrate/MAJOR_PLINY.md` — PLINY-specific: how PLINY recognizes and operates in each mode
- Possibly: extend the directive-authoring template to make mode declaration explicit

## Gauntlet

DAEDALUS + ADA + CATO. Substrate-prose edit. ~60-100 LOC.

## Sequencing

P2. Arc 25 candidate. Bundles with two-team-pattern + memory-as-alignment + multi-team-pattern + handoff-author skill.

## Cross-references

- `substrate/operating-disciplines.md` §10 (HITL/Autonomous) + §11 (autonomous-mode-setup) — existing partial canon to extend
- `substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md` §12 (Mode 1 / Mode 2 framing) — existing partial canon
- Arc 21 directive A4 (mode propagation) — empirical anchor for downward-propagation rule
- `feedback_session_state_continuum_for_sequential_dispatches.md` — related memory on session-state transitions
